clue.text: Nicks and cuts around surgical procedures

indicators.note: the word for cuts goes around the word for operations, enclosing it

parts.note: chops are cuts (of meat, or with an axe)
OPS is short for operations

explanation.surface: A scene of injuries and cuts in a hospital, with nicks and surgical work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nicks' looks like small cuts, but it is British slang for police stations, and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a nick is a police station, and so is a cop shop.

clue.text: Group mostly provide services with kinky orgies

indicators.note: mostly drops the final letter of the word

parts.note: to cater is to provide food and services

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: Caterers for a kinky orgy party.
explanation.definitionFit: To categorise is to sort into groups.

clue.text: Line at bottom of pad: brilliant material

indicators.note: in a down answer, at bottom of puts the line letter under the pad word

parts.note: a pillow is a soft pad
ace means brilliant

explanation.surface: A brilliant line on the bottom of a notepad.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillow lace is a lace fabric made on a cushion with bobbins.

clue.text: That man with talent to make love

parts.note: he refers to that man
art is skill or talent

explanation.surface: A talented man knows how to make love.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart is the seat of affection, so stands for love.

clue.text: Prince going over acts of carrying on; they're taken for granted

indicators.note: in a down answer, going over puts the prince letter above the rest

parts.note: resumptions are acts of continuing again

explanation.surface: A prince reviewing acts of carrying on, which he takes for granted.
explanation.definitionFit: Presumptions are assumptions accepted as true without proof.

clue.text: Escort hugging Bill in darkness

indicators.note: hugging means the escort word wraps round the bill word

parts.note: to show someone to a place is to escort them
AD is short for advertisement, a bill posted up

explanation.surface: An escort embraces someone called Bill in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; here it is a poster, giving AD.
explanation.definitionFit: A shadow is an area of darkness where light is blocked.

clue.text: Handicap stakes around noon: placed at the back, having led

indicators.note: having led puts the rear piece first, ahead of the race

parts.note: hind means at the back

indicators.note: around puts the race word about the noon letter

parts.note: a stakes is a horse race, as in the Derby Stakes

explanation.surface: A horse race report: a handicap where one led but was placed at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed' is a link; 'stakes' is a horse race, not bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance is an obstacle or impediment, a handicap.

clue.text: Wet duck crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means the duck word straddles the river letter

parts.note: to duck is to dip under water

explanation.surface: A duck crossing a river gets wet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' is British for feeble, the noun sense of a drip.
explanation.definitionFit: A drip is a weak, ineffectual person; a wet in British slang.

clue.text: Insignificant duke's a weakling

parts.note: wee is Scottish for tiny, insignificant
D abbreviates duke; the 's is just 'is' linking

explanation.surface: A minor duke is a feeble figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A weed is a puny, weak person.

clue.text: A long time by checkout, prepared spaces for food

parts.note: a till is the cash register at a checkout
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: Waiting a long time at the supermarket checkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is land ploughed and cultivated for growing crops.

clue.text: Home party is private

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
a side is a party in a dispute or game

explanation.surface: A party held at home is a private affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside information is private, known only to a closed circle.

clue.text: Succeeded, Conservative with effective lying

parts.note: S abbreviates succeeded in genealogies
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
a telling blow is an effective one

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician succeeds thanks to effective lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling stories is a euphemism for telling lies.

clue.text: One removes presence of army before raid in Germany

indicators.note: in says the army-and-raid letters sit within the abbreviation for Germany
before puts the army word ahead of the raid word

parts.note: a host is an army or great multitude
a bust is a police raid

explanation.surface: A military raid on Germany that wipes out an enemy's presence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presence' is a ghostly presence: the definition is the film-title job of clearing spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghostbuster is someone who rids a place of spirits, a presence being a spectral being.

clue.text: Short hair on balls goes astray

indicators.note: in a down answer, on puts the hair piece above the balls piece
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: tresses are locks of hair
in football a ball played to a teammate is a pass

explanation.surface: A rude picture of a short hair on testicles.
explanation.definitionFit: To trespass is to sin or stray beyond bounds, as in the Lord's Prayer.

clue.text: Cheats read result out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Cheats in an exam read the result out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheats' sounds like exam fraud; it means unfaithful partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulterers cheat on their spouses.

clue.text: Part of software licence that's old

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An outdated clause in a software licence.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a surviving object from the past, something antique.

clue.text: Left one with money in last casino game? Chip lost

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters have gone astray and been jumbled

explanation.surface: A gambler loses a last chip at the casino tables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' signals the anagram of LAST CASINO GAME CHIP; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A champagne socialist is a wealthy person professing left-wing views.

clue.text: Went with member — anger regularly taken out with roulette bet

parts.note: a part is a member, as of a body

indicators.note: taking out every other letter of the word anger leaves the alternate ones behind

parts.note: a bet on red is a standard roulette bet

explanation.surface: A club member angrily loses a bet at roulette.
explanation.definitionFit: To have partnered someone is to have accompanied them, as at a dance.

clue.text: See 16
Reduce large tripod

parts.note: to ease pressure is to reduce it
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An instruction to shrink a large camera stand.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a three-legged stand for a painter's canvas.

clue.text: One from the back training until team is knocked out

parts.note: PE is physical education, training

indicators.note: knocked out of shape suggests the letters are battered into a new order

explanation.surface: A sports team keeps training until it is knocked out of the cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked out' rearranges UNTIL TEAM into NULTIMATE; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Penultimate means second to last, the one before the final one.

clue.text: One hollow logo on the box

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a dent is a hollow

explanation.surface: A dented logo on a cardboard box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the box' is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: An ident is a TV channel's short logo sequence between programmes.

clue.text: Draws on American king-size cigarettes at last

parts.note: US means American

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of both words

explanation.surface: An American smoker takes drags on king-size cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw on resources is to use them.

clue.text: Strippers primarily round there?

indicators.note: primarily takes the opening letter of the word

parts.note: O is round in shape
ho is a call to draw attention to something over there, as in land ho

explanation.surface: Asking whether strip clubs are found round there.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a London district long known for strip clubs; the whole clue is both wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho, in London's West End, was notorious for strip joints and sex shops.

clue.text: Empty sauce bottles smell cleaner

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, so the outer letters contain the smell
emptying a word leaves only its outer letters

parts.note: pong is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: Emptied sauce bottles that smell and need cleaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge is used to wipe and clean surfaces.

clue.text: Film lover can see it when released

indicators.note: letters released from their order are free to rearrange

explanation.surface: A film buff can catch the movie once it's released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when released' looks like film release; it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A cineaste is a devotee of cinema.

clue.text: Broadcaster getting in hot water

indicators.note: getting in means the hot letter goes inside the broadcaster word

parts.note: a sower broadcasts seed by scattering it by hand
H abbreviates hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A TV broadcaster lands in trouble, in hot water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcaster' suggests TV but is one who scatters seed; 'in hot water' looks like an idiom, yet only 'water' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A shower is a brief fall of rain, so water from the sky.

clue.text: For example, love to sit back with velvet cushions, ultimately puffed-up ones

parts.note: EG abbreviates the Latin for example
love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: back says the word sit is read backwards
ultimately takes the final letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Vain types love lounging on velvet cushions.
explanation.definitionFit: Egotists are conceited people, inflated with self-importance.
